Black Lamborghini Urus S Joins the Low-Riding Squad, Looks Like Bruce Wayne’s Daily
9 photos
Photo: Instagram | rdbla
Lamborghini may have an entirely new Urus in its family, namely the Urus SE Performante. Well, it’s not actually new, but it is fresh, and it is the sole surviving member of the entire lineup. However, the older models still make headlines for different reasons.
Either due to a more or less cool tuning job, an example that was spotted being put through its paces, or one that is searching for a new home on the World Wide Web, these are mainly the things that still put the spotlight on the original Urus, the Urus S, and the Urus Performante. And in this case, we have a very cool-looking (this writer believes) Urus S, which came directly from RDB LA, looking all muscular, and more like a blue-blooded hatch than an exotic crossover.
That is due to the new suspension, which has brought the car’s body a lot closer to the ground. Thus, this Lamborghini Urus S has joined the low-riding squad, and as a result, it looks a lot more aggressive, and also quite confused, to be honest. Still, it is far from being kitschy, isn’t it? Another mod revolves around the wheels, which are significantly bigger than the OEM ones. These are concave, feature a black and silver look, and have a multi-spoke design.
Some tuners would have called it a day after fitting new wheels to a vehicle and fiddling with its suspension. However, the Italian super crossover in question also sports a few other modifications. We didn’t mention the muscular overall look for nothing, because it has fender flares. Thus, it is a lot wider than before. There is also a new apron on deck, as well as new side skirt attachments from what we can tell, though we have to note that that pics shared by RDB LA on its social media channels recently are very dark.
Photo: Instagram | rdbla Just like the crossover itself, for that matter, and the mods do not end here, because this Lamborghini Urus S also features a completely new rear diffuser with a four-fin design. The ducktail spoiler in the middle of the tailgate has also come from the aftermarket world, and so has the wing mounted above the rear windscreen. The front and rear bumpers, on the other hand, as well as the hood, and other elements haven’t been touched with the tuning stick from what we can see.
The pictured machine features a glossy black look on the outside, and has been sprinkled with tinting for the windows and the taillights. In fact, it if had had tinted headlights and black wheels then it would have been a murdered-out proposal. Moreover, a satin paint protection film would have made it look like a veritable fighter jet for the road, but we won’t complain about that, because, as mentioned above, we (or I in this case) think that this is one cool-looking machine.
Bruce Wayne would probably drive it on a regular basis, as it definitely looks like it could blend in with the traffic in Gotham City without breaking a sweat. And that’s a win in our book. Do you know what would have been cool? If we had the chance to take a look inside. But that probably means that the interior hasn’t been modified, with an emphasis on the word “probably.” This Lamborghini Urus S needs a black overall look in the cabin, this writer thinks.
Photo: Instagram | rdbla There is also no word on the powertrain, so the oily bits likely carry over with no changes. This means a twin-turbocharged V8 engine with a 4.0-liter displacement and no electric trickery whatsoever. The Urus S had the exact same output and thrust as the Lamborghini Urus Performante. This means 666 ps (490 kW/657 hp) and 850 Nm (627 pound-feet) of torque. The 0-100 kph (0-62 mph) sprint takes 3.5 seconds, and that makes it two-tenths of a second slower than its more track-focused sibling, the Performante.
Lamborghini’s Urus S pretty much prioritized luxury over handling and performance, and in case you forgot, it came out a little over four years ago as the direct successor to the pre-facelifted iteration. The Performante was already on sale when the Raging Bull pulled the covers off the S, and now, both of them are officially dead and buried. And so is the plug-in hybrid SE, for that matter, because the SE Performante is the only Urus that remains on sale.
The latter model weighs almost 2.5 metric tons (5,452 pounds), and has a 60 km (37 miles) range on the WLTP cycle. The plug-in hybrid powertrain produces 812 ps (597 kW /801 hp) and 1,000 Nm (738 lb-ft) of torque in total, allowing it to hit 100 kph (62 mph) in 3.3 seconds. That’s just as fast as the non-electrified Performante. The top speed is 312 kph (194 mph). Lambo’s Urus SE Performante has an Estimated MSRP of roughly $320,000. First-Ever BMW X9 Shies Away From Neue Klasse Styling in Fantasy Land, Adopts a Land Yacht Persona
6 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
According to basically every source from across the rumor mill, the premium German automaker from Bavaria, BMW , is considering something big. More precisely, even the automaker recently revealed that it is considering a model sitting above the current BMW X7 flagship three-row crossover SUV, focused on the North American market.
That’s no surprise, of course, after the ailing rival from Ingolstadt, Audi, sequentially revealed not only the third-generation Audi Q7 crossover but also its new larger twin, the first-ever, all-new Audi Q9. BMW has previously hinted at models larger than the X7, and its dealers from America are very happy about it, as it would become available to compete not only with the Mercedes-Benz GLS or Audi Q9 but also the likes of Cadillac Escalade, Lincoln Navigator, Infiniti QX80, and Land Rover Range Rover.
Nothing is official yet, of course, but a new flagship SUV is increasingly likely to arrive before the end of the decade. The company would have additional leverage in North America , where buyers continue to love the humongous trucks and truck-derived SUVs, and BMW’s Spartanburg, South Carolina factory would be the perfect location to manufacture it and avoid the hefty tariffs.
Naturally, since it’s still a rumor and we haven’t seen any prototypes out in the open just yet, no one should expect the new hulking SUV to arrive before the end of the decade, with BMW already holding the rights to the X9 nameplate and it even secured the XB9 moniker, suggesting that an Alpina version might also be on the way.
BMW currently has two platform options to underpin the new model: Neue Klasse, the dedicated EV setup, and the ongoing Cluster Architecture (CLAR). The latter seems more likely since it allows greater flexibility with all types of powertrains and Americans don’t particularly love EVs right now too much. How about the design?
Well, that’s anyone’s guess because it’s too early to have any tell-tale signs, but that’s never a problem for the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the rumored BMW X9.
So, his latest unofficial, hypothetical design project seeks to find out more about the design of the upcoming flagship SUV. Curiously, the pixel master completely abandons Neue Klasse – there’s no sight of the EV architecture because the model is ICE but also there are no styling elements borrowed from there. Instead, this SUV carves its own path, looking like a land yacht with its 3D V-shaped kidney grille.
So, what do you think of this idea – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by CAR DESIGN | RENDERINGS (@kelsonik)

This Dodge Challenger Costs a Lot Less Than You Probably Think
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors
With Dodge’s modern-day muscle car finally tapping into its V8 side for the first time, with production expected to commence in late 2027, arriving as a 2028 model, it is now probably time to finally get that cool Challenger that you’ve been dreaming of for years.
You know what they say, every muscle car is the right muscle car as long as it has a V8 engine under the hood. And the third-gen Challenger certainly ticked this box. After all, the SRT Demon 170 remains the most powerful and fastest of its kind, boasting a whopping 1,025 horsepower (764 kW/1,039 ps) and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque in its range-topping configuration.
With E85 in the tank, a skilled driver behind the wheel, perfect conditions, and a bit of luck, it will rocket to 60 mph (97 kph) in just 1.66 seconds . The quarter mile is dealt with in 8.91 seconds, officially, with an exit speed of just over 151 mph (243+ kph). And under the hood lies a heavily upgraded version of the familiar Hellcat lump, a .6.2-liter V8 engine, in case you forgot.
Dodge offered numerous versions of the Challenger SRT Hellcat over the years, including some that boasted over 800 horsepower with zero outside intervention. This engine also made its way under the hood of the Challenger’s four-door sibling, the previous-gen Charger, and it is reportedly the mill that might eventually power the modern-day Charger, too.
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors The third-gen Dodge Challenger was also offered with a 6.4-liter HEMI V8, a 6.1-liter HEMI V8, and a 5.7-liter HEMI V8. The Pentastar V6 was also a thing in the lesser flavors, and guess what? It is the engine that powers the pictured Dodge Challenger. That’s right, instead of putting the spotlight on yet another Hellcat, a Demon, or a Demon 170, we decided to focus on something that sits, or better said sat, at the bottom of the muscle car food chain.
As we already told you, the firepower is supplied by a 3.6-liter Pentastar V6 engine in this case, which was originally rated at 303 brake horsepower (307 ps/225 kW) and 268 pound-feet (363 Nm) of torque. That’s a mere fraction compared to the Hellcats, not to mention the insane Demon 170. The peak output is available at 6,350 rpm, so you will have to work out the engine, and the maximum thrust at 4,800 rpm.
Depending on the configuration, this model was available either with rear-wheel drive or with an all-wheel drive system, and the latter was an option. In both cases, an eight-speed automatic transmission delivered everything to the wheels. So, is the pictured Dodge Challenger GT RWD or AWD? Your guess is as good as ours, as the vendor, @mxo.motors on Instagram, hasn’t revealed this information.
In fact, the used car dealer behind this muscle car hasn’t said much about it. The vehicle sports a glossy black look from bumper to bumper, has tinted windows all around, and rides on black wheels. The SRT logo on the grille is there for show and tell purposes only. There are a few chrome details on deck for a bit of contrast, and if it weren’t for these, then this would have been a murdered-out proposal. Not that we are complaining or anything, because this machine definitely looks great, doesn’t it?
Photo: Instagram | mxo.motors For what it’s worth, it looks like it is always ready for a quarter-mile brawl, though due to the V6 Pentastar engine that powers it, it obviously won’t put its money where its mouth is. The cockpit is mostly black, with a few gray touches, and features fabric upholstery that has seen better days, at least when it comes to the drive’s seat. The pillars and headliner are black, the usual infotainment system is on deck, and we can also see the SRT logo on the steering wheel, and the fact that it has as an Alpine sound system.
According to the vendor, the Dodge Challenger GT in question is a 2023 model year, and in case you forgot, this was the final model year of the muscle car, which finally left the assembly line at the Brampton facility in Ontario, Canada, making room for its successor, the new-gen Charger.
The Challenger was offered strictly as a two-door coupe, and fought its main rivals from Ford and Chevrolet, the Mustang and Camaro, respectively, and the latter is dead and buried, for now anyway, because it will reportedly return to the automotive world as a four-door sedan only, with V8 firepower and probably a stick shift option for more driving engagement.
Now, despite looking quite fresh, for the most part, this Dodge Challenger has seen a lot of action. The odo reads around 73,000 miles (~117,500 km). As for the asking price, it was $16,700 at the time of writing. But is it worth it? You be the judge of that, and feel free to leave your impressions on this muscle car in the comments box below. Freelander Type 01 Design Project Looks Better Than the Actual Jaguar, Proving Issues With the EV
6 photos
Photo: KDesign AG / Instagram
Have you seen the latest problems the one-percenters face across the automotive industry? They have to choose between the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe and its new SUV counterpart, the Ferrari Luce, or the new Jaguar Type 01 when they want a high-performance EV model that isn’t American or Chinese.
Tough times for them, right? That’s especially true since the days of the teardrop-shaped smooth electric sedan are apparently gone together with the Tesla Model S and only the Lucid Air is left alone to fend off for itself. Now, the battlefield is occupied by weird Chinese EV models and the wacky EV rivals from Westerners that are trying not to copy them… too much.
Anyway, the latest addition to the expanding roster of high-end EV limousines is Jaguar’s most powerful road car in history, the Type 01, a dramatically styled liftback sedan that mixes glamorous industrial-style design with a truly high-performance electric powertrain and cool chassis elements.
The British automaker Jaguar decided to reinvent itself around two years ago, slowly ended production of all previous nameplates, and, since then, ‘groomed’ all of us to prepare for the arrival of the Type 01 with the Type 00 grand touring coupe. Now, the brand’s reinvention is underway with this new four-seat grand tourer, featuring three electric motors and 1,016 horsepower plus 1,007 pound-feet of torque.
The luxury sedan can sprint to 62 mph in 3.2 seconds, has perfect 50:50 weight distribution, and the EV model also comes with an evolved 850-volt architecture with a 118-kWh battery pack that’s said to be good for up to 450 miles of range (WLTP) and up to 320 miles at highway speeds. With a length of 206.4 inches, a height of just 55.24 inches, and no rear window, it’s also a massive design statement.
However, just like with the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe or the Ferrari Luce and unlike the Lucid Air, we’re not sure if the new Jaguar Type 01 stands out in the right or wrong kind of crowds. Initially, the hype has been positive, with 50k expressions of interest, but who knows if all of them will translate into firm purchases?
Anyway, our problem is simple – the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have quickly shown us the issue: automakers today strive for individuality but actually lack personality. So, one of these pixel masters quickly proceeded to imagine an unofficial, hypothetical Land Rover Range Rover sedan design project based directly on the Type 01’s design ethos.
As it turns out, this style is clearly interchangeable with the other member of the JLR family… with just a few modifications. Now, a second CGI expert, Kleber Silva, a Brazil-based virtual artist known as " KDesign AG " on social media, has also decided to have a CGI go at imagining the British-Chinese version of the Jaguar Type 01, remixing it under the new Freelander banner.
The result is startingly direct: the new car brand owned by the Chery Jaguar Land Rover joint venture, which has so far only announced the Freelander 8 full-size SUV , could easily make the Jaguar Type 01 their own with the SUV’s headlights and a few changes to the front and rear fascias. Additionally, the most logical style of the Type 01 also comes with a rear window, not just a panel… So, what do you think – yay or nay? 2026 Paris Motor Show • Project KO11 Is Proof That Geely Wants To "Knock Out" Range Rover, Launches Next Year in Europe
Car Nut Flipped Classics for Decades, Finally Finds Holy Grail Buick GNX, Kneels Before It
51 photos
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins
In the automotive underworld of 1987, a sinister coal-black phantom prowled American boulevards, striking terror into the hearts of European supercar royalty. Cloaked in formal Detroit sheet metal, this turbocharged executioner was so violently quick that its own creators forbade it from being test-driven on public roads. You already guessed it’s the one and only Buick GNX – Detroit’s last true muscle car.
For 39 years, one of these dark legends slumbered in climate-controlled secrecy, hiding a bizarre assembly-line anomaly beneath its shadowy, menacing tail. The lure of finally capturing this elusive beast pulled veteran car hunter Dennis Collins out of bed at 3:45 in the morning.
Documenting the chase on his YouTube channel, the Texas collector admitted that despite buying and selling thousands of classics, this specific model had always escaped his grasp. Joined by his trusted mechanic Alex Bohling and cameraman Zach Gorgas, Dennis embarked on a 501-mile trek from Wylie, Texas, toward Pelican State.
At 11:20 in the morning, the team rolled into Madisonville, Louisiana, where longtime friend and scout Jay Riecke had tracked down the prize at Pellegrini Performance Group. Shop owner Jay Pellegrini III welcomed the crew into his sprawling automotive sanctuary, home to over 50 machines ranging from 1940s classics to 2026 race cars.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins However, the main stage was reserved exclusively for the 1987 Buick GNX number #192. Even the famously stoic Alex Bohling broke into a wide grin at the sight of the time capsule coupe, which displayed a mere 1,528 miles on its Stewart-Warner analog speedometer. Its owner bought the car in 2021 and fitted replica wheels, yet guilt struck after just eight miles, prompting four years of storage.
Popping the trunk revealed a treasure trove of provenance that slingshots the coupe into the highest echelons of collector pieces. Alongside the hardcover history book and build sheets sat the original window sticker confirming a $29,290 retail price, which the first buyer paid without markup when taking delivery in 1988 with 28.1 miles on the clock.
Better still, the backseat held the original Molly Designs jacket serialized to car 192. General Motors single-stage black paint from the late 1980s was notoriously flawed from the factory, yet this specimen gleamed after a gentle polish. Digital paint meter readings registered an even 3.5 to 4.5 mils down the flanks, verifying untouched factory lacquer.
Beneath the hood, the ceramic-coated Garrett T-3 turbocharger housing and intercooler look pristine, accompanied by the electric hydro-boost brake system.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins While driving to Louisiana, Dennis Collins had telephoned a former ASC/McLaren technician who helped engineer and assemble these cars in 1987. The insider divulged that workers initially road-tested the coupes around Livonia, Michigan, until police intervened and General Motors dropped the hammer.
Banned from public roads, ASC/McLaren installed a Clayton in-floor rolling dynamometer, running every car for a simulated nine miles, though several cars launched off the rollers into the wall. Bad rollers? Badass cars, more like it.
Hoisting the coupe onto post lift exposed an undercarriage still bearing factory chalk marks, suspension tags, and date-coded Goodyear Eagle Gatorback tires on 16-inch mesh wheels. Inspecting the bespoke rear torque arm and Panhard bar, Dennis Collins spotted a stunning anomaly stamped into the cast-aluminum GNX differential cover.
Although documented as number #192, its untouched axle cover bore serial number #193; workers inadvertently swapped covers during assembly. No two ways about it, since there were no reproduction housings made (and stamped with the car’s serial number from the production run).
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Thrilled by the factory quirk and offering to swap covers with whoever owns car #193 (and/or who has diff cover for #192), Dennis Collins paid the full asking price, and got the reproduction wheels, and the car cover as a bonus.
While corporate literature translated it as Grand National eXperimental, ASC/McLaren technicians famously insisted the X stood for X-rated due to its ferocious street manners. That reputation marked the final, defiant crescendo of a mechanical lineage stretching back more than 25 years.
The bloodline began in 1961 when Buick introduced its 3.2-liter Fireball V6 engine, followed in 1973 by the launch of the upscale Regal personal luxury coupe. Forced induction arrived at the 1976 Indianapolis 500, where a turbocharged 3.8-liter V6 Regal paced the race, spawning the mass-produced 1978 Buick Regal Sport Coupe.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins After sleeker Regal coupes captured consecutive manufacturer championships in the 1981 and 1982 NASCAR Winston Cup Grand National Series, Buick unveiled the Regal Grand National in February 1982. Initially carrying a naturally aspirated 4.1-liter V6 making 125 horsepower, the model returned in 1984 in all-black trim with a turbocharged 3.8-liter V6 producing 200 horsepower.
Adding an air-to-air intercooler boosted output to 235 horsepower in 1986 and 245 horsepower by 1987.
With the rear-wheel-drive G-body platform slated for retirement in favor of front-wheel-drive architecture after 1987, Buick commissioned ASC/McLaren to build an ultimate swan song of the turbo Buicks. Loaded Grand Nationals were pulled from the Flint assembly line and shipped to Livonia for transformation.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Although advertisements touted an exclusive run for the Fortunate 500, 547 top-tier dealerships met General Motors' strict allocation quotas (when the 47 excluded dealers threatened legal action, Buick built gave in and assembled 547 units).
To create the monster, ASC/McLaren upgraded the 3.8-liter V6 with a Garrett AiResearch T-3 turbocharger featuring a lightweight ceramic impeller that slashed turbo lag. Engineers installed a larger ceramic-coated intercooler, a reprogrammed engine computer raising boost to 15 PSI, and free-flowing dual exhausts.
Power routed through a recalibrated Turbo Hydramatic 200-4R 4-speed automatic transmission to a chassis sporting fender louvers, composite flares, and staggered 16-inch tires.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Official spec sheets claimed 276 horsepower at 4,400 rpm and 360 lb-ft of torque at 3,000 rpm, but dynamometer tests proved the engine actually produced over 300 horsepower and 420 lb-ft. Weighing 3,540 pounds, the GNX rocketed from 0 to 60 miles per hour in 4.6 seconds and cleared the quarter-mile in 13.2 seconds at 104 miles per hour, before reaching a governed top speed of 124 miles per hour.
Combining an $18,295 well-optioned Grand National with the $10,995 ASC/McLaren package yielded a $29,290 sticker, more than double the $11,976 base price of a standard 110-horsepower 1987 Buick Regal. That premium was more than worth it, as it utterly humiliated corporate G-body rivals.
Oldsmobile's 1987 Cutlass Supreme 442 packed a 170-horsepower 5.0-liter V8 requiring 8.5 seconds to hit 60 miles per hour, while Chevrolet's 180-horsepower 5.0-liter Monte Carlo SS Aerocoupe needed 7.8 seconds and ran 15.9-second quarter-miles.
Photo: YouTube/Dennis Collins Across the broader Detroit landscape, no domestic muscle car or sports car could match the brick-shaped Buick off the line. In 1987, the flagship 240-horsepower 5.7-liter Chevrolet Corvette needed 5.7 seconds to reach 60 miles per hour, the 225-horsepower 5.0-liter Ford Mustang GT required 6.2 seconds, and the 215-horsepower 5.7-liter Pontiac Trans Am GTA took 6.4 seconds. Chevrolet only caught it when the 375-horsepower Lotus-engineered Corvette ZR-1 arrived in 1990.
Even thoroughbred European exotics suffered humiliation at the stoplight against this six-cylinder giant killer. The Buick out-launched the 282-horsepower Porsche 911 Turbo at 4.9 seconds to 60 miles per hour, the 382-horsepower Lamborghini Countach 5000 QV at 4.8 seconds, and the 260-horsepower Ferrari 328 GTS at 5.8 seconds.
Only the arrival of the $400,000, 471-horsepower Ferrari F40 in July 1987 ended the reign of the darkest outlaw Detroit ever unleashed. And don’t tell me history is fair, because look at what an F40 is worth today (despite being vastly more numerous, at 1,315 examples). And don’t even get me started on the Hemi Cudas, also more abundant than the one-year-only Buick GNX.

Genius Installs CarPlay on First-Gen Amazon Echo Show Because Why Not
18 photos
Photo: reddit user ARJeepGuy123
People have been looking for cheap ways to get CarPlay in their cars for many years, and it now appears that there’s a new way to do it. Maybe not in the most convenient way, that’s true, but trying it out won’t cost you anything.
Someone has managed to get CarPlay up and running on a first-gen Amazon Echo Show 5, turning the device into a wireless Apple CarPlay unit. That’s right, the device you probably almost threw away can now run CarPlay, and the process of setting up everything isn’t the most complex.
It’s all possible thanks to LineageOS and an application called DiPlay.
Amazon’s devices ship with FireOS, so the first thing you must do is get rid of this operating system and install LineageOS. Once you do this, you get access to a whole new world, but if you want to stick with the CarPlay dream, you need to install DiPlay.
This application has a very simple purpose: enable CarPlay on an Android device, and best of all, it offers both wired and wireless connections. This means that you won’t even need to connect your iPhone with a cable to run CarPlay on the Echo.
Don’t imagine that you’ll get the same experience as on a native or factory-installed CarPlay head unit . Not at all, but at first glance, you’ll get audio, wireless connections, and several other big things that would otherwise cost high dollars.
The user who did this explains on reddit that downgrading to an earlier version of DiPlay was necessary due to a music bug. On the other hand, the music is playing correctly directly through the Echo’s speakers, but if you want, you can also connect another stereo system to the device using the audio jack, so eventually, you can turn the Echo into a media player running Spotify or any other app supported by CarPlay.
Such a project is fun and exciting for those who were looking for a new use for their aging Echos, but in reality, you’ll still want to get a real-deal CarPlay unit if you want to enjoy Apple’s system in your car. Nothing beats a factory-installed unit or an aftermarket media receiver with CarPlay support - not long ago, Sony revealed that it’s leaving this market , so if you’re searching for such an upgrade, you’d better decide on your purchase ASAP.
The full instructions to get everything up and running are available here, but keep in mind that you could come across various bugs that might require further steps to deal with. However, considering the first-gen Echo can’t be used for many things these days (though I do recommend that you replace FireOS with LineageOS to breathe new life into your Echo), giving CarPlay a go is a good choice.

How Much Is a 2022 Ferrari F8 Spider Worth After 8,000 Miles?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec
Even though it hasn’t been a thing at Ferrari for the past three years, the F8 still looks very modern, and has aged like fine wine, just like pretty much every other exotic model the company has signed over the decades.
Production lasted for a very short time, especially in supercar years, as the F8 saw the light of day only between 2019 and 2023. By comparison, its predecessor, the 488, was made between 2015 and 2020, and the 458 that came before it, and some consider to be the last real Ferrari, as it had no electric trickery and zero forced induction, was assembled from 2009 to 2015. Further back, the F8 can trace its roots to the F430, 360, F355, 348, and so on.
As for its modern-day equivalent, it is called the 296 , and came out in 2022 when it comes to the Coupe, whereas the Spider debuted the following year. It features an electrified 3.0-liter V6 engine with a total system output of 819 hp (830 ps/610 kW). It takes 2.9 seconds to deal with 0-62 mph (0-100 kph), has a top speed exceeding 205 mph (330 kph), returns the equivalent of mpg US (8.3 l/100 km) combined, and has a zero-emission range of 15 miles (25 km).
The Prancing Horse is preparing an even more extreme version of the 296 as we speak, and word on the street is that it might not feature any electric trickery whatsoever. You can check it out here as a pre-production tester, though preferably after you keep reading this story, which is all about the Ferrari F8 pictured in the gallery. As you can clearly see, it is a Spider, which is Ferrari slang for open-top, and from what we can tell, it hasn’t been visited by the tuning fairy.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec Things such as the front bumper, apron, front hood, side skirts, vent trim on the rear three-quarter panels, integrated ducktail spoiler, rear bumper, diffuser, exhaust tips, and even the wheels are stock. The ground clearance looks the same, so the suspension hasn’t been tweaked either, and this machine sports a red paint finish on the outside, and offers a combination of black leather, gray Alcantara, red stitching, and metal and carbon fiber trim on the inside.
As for the firepower, it is supplied by a V8 engine. That’s right, unlike its successor, the 296, the Ferrari F8 still had an eight-cylinder engine mounted behind the passenger compartment. The mill is twin-turbocharged, and has a 3.9-liter displacement, and, according to the official spec sheet, it produces 710 hp (530 kW/720 ps) at 8,000 rpm, and 568 pound-feet (770 Nm) of torque available at 3,250 rpm.
Are you curious about the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration? Well, with no outside intervention, the Ferrari F8 Spider can complete the sprint in 2.9 seconds. That’s two-tenths of a second slower than the Temerario, which is Lamborghini’s new “baby” supercar that replaced the Huracan, hitting production in 2025. Both the F8 Tributo (Coupe) and F8 Spider (Convertible) were equally fast to 62 mph, and has an identical top speed of 311 mph (340 kph), which is higher than the 296’s.
Photo: Instagram | limitedspec Some of the features mentioned in the ad, because the pictured Ferrari F8 Spider is for sale in the United States of America, include the carbon fiber racing seats, Scuderia shields, nose-lift kit to better clear speed bumps and steep driveways, and a few other things. This Italian supercar is a 2022 model, according to the vendor, and as mentioned above, production of the F8 ceased entirely in 2023.
What else should you know about it? Well, it is located in Miami, Florida, and has around 8,000 miles (almost 13,000 km) on the clock, as mentioned in the title. Thus, it hasn’t seen that much action over the years, as the mileage is more than decent for such a thing.
You are likely wondering about the Benjamins, but before revealing how much this thing costs, we will remind you that a used Ferrari F8 will set you back a minimum of $380,000 in today’s used car market in the States. The F8 Tributo, aka the fixed-roof variant, typically sells from the high-$300K to roughly $500K, and the F8 Spider, the convertible, fetches from around $400K to over $700K. The latter number is reserved for rare and low-mileage examples.
So, how much do you think you will have to fork out if you want to write your name on the dotted line in this case? Unless you said $579,980, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price of the pictured supercar at the time of writing. The vehicle was advertised by @limitedspec on social media, and you know what to do next if you really want this Ferrari F8 Spider , don’t you? But is this thing really worth almost $600K?
